nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Which aspect of the movement does the paper seek to outline through its analysis?
nodes.answer: The paper seeks to outline convergences and tensions within the movement related to alternative currencies and degrowth.
nodes.paragraph: Our goal in this paper is to analyse how this movement that has been increasing its presence not only within the academic realm (Engler et al. 2024; Farooq 2024), but also among policy- making international debates and reports (Parrique et al. 2019; Parrique 2022) conceptualises the role and place of alternative currencies in the transformation of socio-eco- nomic relations towards a more sustainable and inclusive society. We explore the literature on degrowth through criti- cal analysis of the way it refers to alternative currencies, by drawing out proposals and pathways from its positioning on the subject, and by outlining convergences and tensions within the movement. Informed by debates within the move- ment, we seek to set a prospective research agenda located at the crossroad of these two fields: alternative currencies and degrowth. To meet the aims of the paper, we first review defini- tions and typologies of alternative currencies and describe the emergence and development of alternative currency projects worldwide (Sect. nodes.question: What is the primary focus of the degrowth movement as mentioned in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The primary focus of the degrowth movement is on alternative currencies and their role in socio-ecological transformations.

We next propose questions for future research that debates within the degrowth movement high- light as relevant to a better understanding of the role and design of alternative currencies and monetary systems in socio-ecological transformations (Sect. "Towards a prospec - tive research agenda"). The paper ends with reflections and conclusions (Sect. "Conclusions"). Alternative or complementary currencies? We use the adjective alternative to describe currencies that aim to transform territories and make society , to use the French subtitle of Marie Fare's (2016) book. According to Blanc (2018), alternative currencies are first and foremost monetary devices that are conceived with a view to socio- economic transformation. The use of the adjective socio- economic implies for Blanc that these devices assemble a variety of tools and rules to guide the practices of users in order to achieve an ethical project Of course, there are other qualifiers in the universe of currencies with a voca- tion of socio-economic transformation.
